correctness.rationale: For every integer q>=3, every integer L_i>=1, and every real μ>0, 4I-B_L is exactly positive by a sum-of-squares identity. The Schur complement F(λ) decreases strictly above 4; its explicit value at 4 proves the trichotomy and excludes multiple above-band modes. The exact finite-branch root and strict concavity of h_L in arm length prove balanced/extreme layout ordering at each λ>4. Geometric transfer convergence gives q^2/[μ(q-μ)] for μ<q/2. Direct finite-matrix eigensolutions independently check 218 band-edge, 1308 mode count, 254 balancing, 616 root and 24 limit diagnostics. These are diagnostics, not finite-only proof.

originality.rationale: The directly relevant complete source arXiv:1112.4526, Secs 2–4, proves an unweighted starlike-tree localization theorem and contains the μ=1 instance, which is acknowledged rather than claimed. Full arXiv:1104.4280 Secs 1–2 prove majorization for unweighted Laplacian coefficients, not the mass-loaded threshold or the ordering of the weighted generalized above-band eigenvalue. The novelty asserted is the exact hub-mass cutoff, all arm-profile design extremizers and frequency ordering for arbitrary positive central-to-arm mass ratio. Targeted published-results searches revealed only quantum-graph and continuous-metric-star comparators with different operators and claims. The 2005 mass–spring scale-free-network paper is an identified abstract-only priority risk; failed retrieval is not used to infer noncoverage.
residual_risks: Earlier spectral-graph theory may contain an implicit general mass-weighted starlike root equation; no exhaustive historical survey is claimed.
The full text of Iguchi–Yamada (2005) was not inspected, so specialized finite-star formula priority cannot be categorically excluded.
Some unweighted spectral-radius and grafting order results could imply the μ=1 special case; that special case is explicitly excluded from novelty claims.

value.rationale: Mode localization beyond the one-dimensional bulk band is a meaningful topological and mass-contrast effect. At fixed branch count and total masses, an exact optimizer and anti-optimizer determine the largest allowable junction mass that still permits the mode, and order the actual above-band frequency. For three arms and nine arm masses, choosing (3,3,3) versus (7,1,1) turns an isolated mode on/off at exactly the same hub mass ratio 6/5 and total spring budget. The theorem is a complete, nontrivial allocation classification, not a numerical sample or a rephrasing of the established equal-mass result.
